study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective longitudinal study
exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal birth vs. cesarean delivery)
outcome: Perineal complex components (perineal membrane, perineal body, levator ani) evaluated by 3-dimensional endovaginal ultrasound
Presence or absence of the Hourglass-Band pattern
cohort: The study included 126 postpartum women at high risk for pelvic floor injury.
finding: The altered Hourglass-Band pattern is an imaging abnormality strongly associated with vaginal birth, distinct from levator ani avulsion and anal sphincter laceration.
mod_finding: The Hourglass-Band pattern was altered in 45% of women with a vaginal delivery, significantly more often than in the 16% observed in the cesarean delivery control group, and its features were 2.4 to 4.1 times more likely to be absent after vaginal birth.
